package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: LokiBot is a credential-stealing malware distributed primarily via phishing emails. It is designed to extract sensitive information such as usernames, passwords, and banking credentials from infected systems by targeting browser, email, and FTP client storage. The malware exfiltrates this data to attacker-controlled command-and-control (C2) servers, enabling unauthorized access and financial theft.

execution_context.trigger: Upon execution of the malicious attachment (user opens the phishing email attachment)
execution_context.file_location: Malicious executable or script delivered as an email attachment, typically located in the user's Downloads or email client temporary directory
required_permissions: filesystem (read access to credential storage locations)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The code enumerates credential storage locations for browsers (e.g., Chrome, Firefox), email clients (e.g., Outlook, Thunderbird), and FTP clients (e.g., FileZilla), extracts stored usernames and passwords, and sends the collected data to a remote command-and-control server via HTTP POST requests.
malicious_snippets.code_language: C/C++ (typical for LokiBot payloads, as identified in malware analysis reports)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution of the malicious attachment, the code enumerates browser, email, and FTP credential storage locations, extracts stored usernames and passwords, and exfiltrates this data to a remote C2 server via HTTP POST requests, resulting in credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code systematically accesses credential storage locations for multiple applications and transmits sensitive data to an external server without user knowledge or consent. This automated credential harvesting and exfiltration is a hallmark of information stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not access and transmit stored credentials from browsers, email clients, or FTP clients without explicit user consent and clear user interaction. Such behavior is only expected in password managers or backup tools with transparent user approval and secure handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Password managers may access credential stores, but only after explicit user authentication and never transmit credentials to unknown or untrusted servers. Backup tools may access such data, but with user configuration and secure, trusted destinations.
key_indicators: Automated access to browser, email, and FTP credential storage files (e.g., Login Data, signons.sqlite, FileZilla.xml)
Process spawned from an email client or opened attachment accessing credential files
Outbound HTTP POST requests to hardcoded or suspicious C2 domains/IPs immediately after execution
Creation of temporary files in user profile or temp directories during credential extraction
No user interface or notification during credential access and exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing email with a malicious attachment, often disguised as a business document (e.g., invoice, purchase order).
Victim opens the attachment, triggering execution of the LokiBot payload.
LokiBot enumerates and extracts stored credentials from browsers, email clients, and FTP clients by accessing their respective storage files.
Stolen credentials and sensitive data are sent to the attacker's command-and-control server via HTTP POST requests.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to victim's accounts and sensitive information

behavioral_signatures: Process spawned from an email client or opened attachment accessing browser, email, or FTP credential storage files
Outbound HTTP POST requests to known or suspicious LokiBot C2 domains/IPs immediately after opening an email attachment
Execution of unknown or unsigned binaries/scripts from email client temporary or Downloads folders
Creation of temporary files in user profile or temp directories during credential extraction
file_indicators: Executable attachments with double extensions (e.g., invoice.pdf.exe, order.doc.scr)
Unknown or unsigned executables/scripts appearing in email client temp folders (e.g., %AppData%\Local\Temp, /tmp/)
Temporary files created in user profile directories during credential extraction (e.g., %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Temp\*.tmp)
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to hardcoded or known LokiBot C2 domains/IPs (as identified in threat intelligence feeds)
Unusual outbound connections to external IPs or domains immediately after execution of an email attachment
Network traffic with user-agent strings or HTTP headers characteristic of LokiBot variants
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes spawned from email clients or opened attachments that access credential storage files (e.g., browser Login Data, email client databases, FTP config files) and initiate outbound HTTP POST requests to suspicious or known LokiBot C2 infrastructure. Flag execution of attachments with suspicious file extensions (e.g., .pdf.exe) or from untrusted sources. Correlate file, process, and network activity with threat intelligence on LokiBot indicators. Alert on creation of temporary files in user profile or temp directories during credential extraction.
